stem:
Eshan sees mosquito larvae in stagnant water. A thin, transparent layer of kerosene on the water surface can stop them becoming adults. The layer looks shiny.

Why does the kerosene layer work?

options.text: It makes the water look shiny, so adult mosquitoes refuse to lay eggs.
Larvae must reach air at the surface to breathe; the kerosene film blocks that air contact.
Adult mosquitoes must dive under the kerosene to breathe, so the layer kills flying adults.
Kerosene is transparent, so air still reaches the larvae and breathing is unchanged.

teacher.key_rationale: Larvae need surface air. The kerosene film blocks that contact.
